$comment: The Luz design tokens, in one place and in no platform's language (ADR-0031, DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §3).
tooling/scripts/generate_design_tokens.py turns this into the Android token file; the Apple apps read the same
values when they arrive (Phase 11-12), so the two platforms cannot drift apart by hand-editing one of them.
Colours are sRGB hex. Sizes are density-independent (dp/pt) and text sizes scale with the platform's text setting.

color.$comment: Near-black surfaces, a muted neutral text ramp, and the Luz amber used only as an accent.

bgSurface3.use: the surface under a focused item

lineSubtle.use: hairlines, track behind a progress bar

textPrimary.use: titles and anything that must be read at 3 m

textTertiary.use: captions and counts — white at about 40 %

accent.use: primary actions, selection, focus ring, progress
accent.$comment: Sampled from the owner's logo (hue 28, the mark's core amber) and lightened until it reads on #0B0D10: 9.4:1 against the base, and near-black text on it passes comfortably.

accentPressed.use: the accent while a control is being pressed

onAccent.use: text and icons drawn on top of the accent

stateLive.use: the live marker and the now-line in the guide

focusRing.use: the hairline around a focused card, under the lift
focusRing.$comment: White at low opacity, not amber. The owner chose the Apple TV app as the reference: there, focus is a lift — scale, a soft shadow, a brighter surface — and colour stays in the artwork. The amber is still the app's accent: progress, selection, the primary action.

scrimTop.use: the transparent end of a gradient laid over artwork

scrimBottom.use: the solid end of that gradient, matching the background

material.$comment: Surfaces are not grey paint: they are white or black laid over whatever is behind them, at an opacity, with a hairline of white to catch the edge. That is how the Apple TV app gets depth without drawing boxes, and it is why a panel over artwork still shows the artwork.

panel.use: a menu or a settings pane: dark, and the screen behind it still shows through

raised.use: a resting card or row: white laid on very faintly

raisedFocused.use: the same surface under the remote

hairline.use: the one-pixel edge that separates a panel from what is behind it

scrim.use: what dims the screen behind a menu

text.$comment: Roles, not fonts. Each platform uses its own system typeface (Android: the platform sans; Apple: SF).

display.use: one number or word on a screen of its own

body.use: the smallest size for anything that must be read from a sofa

space.$comment: A 4-point scale. Names are the multiplier.

safeHorizontal.use: TV overscan margin, left and right

safeVertical.use: TV overscan margin, top and bottom

motion.$comment: Short enough that the interface never feels like it is waiting for itself.

focus.$comment: Focus is a lift: the card grows, rises on a soft shadow and brightens. The hairline is a whisper under it, not an outline — it reads on a washed-out panel without turning the screen into a set of boxes.
